reason: Holds. _sections_from_payload only accepts payload['sections'] as a list (a dict of section strings yields 0 sections), and _insider_rows_from_payload skips every row without transaction_date/trade_date and reads the issuer from issuer_name/company_name, so the upstream filing-level Form-4 rows and top-level 'name' are all dropped. reason: Holds. The yfinance timeframe map requests '30m' with a '3mo' lookback, beyond Yahoo's 60-day intraday window, so every 30m request comes back empty. The history route turns that empty series into a 200 with provider 'none' and, for IN, reason 'in_eod_only'. ChartPanel maps that reason to the 'BSE/NSE serve end-of-day only' copy, even though 15m loads for the same symbol.
evidence_checked: Read the timeframe map, the empty-series downgrade and the chart's empty-state copy. Re-ran GETs on :52152.
repro_check: curl ':52152/history/SPY?timeframe=30m' -> 0 bars, provider none, reason null; RELIANCE.NS 30m -> 0 bars, reason in_eod_only; SPY 15m -> 546 bars (yfinance); RELIANCE.NS 15m -> 522 bars. Reproduced.

reason: The core claim holds: _label_series_freshness feeds bars[-1].timestamp (the period-start date for yfinance) to freshness_for with a 3-session tolerance, so the current monthly bar is badged 'stale' and the chart adds a 'Stale data' session label. Correction: the chart never renders 'EOD as of <future date>'. ChartPanel mounts StalenessBadge without asOf, so an eod series shows a plain 'EOD' and 'Market closed'. reason: Holds. _greeks_fd takes gamma as a second difference of CRR tree NPVs with a 1%-of-spot bump. A CRR price is piecewise-linear in spot between node crossings, so the stencil measures tree discretisation: 2.82x Black-Scholes at the panel's default 200 steps, and 0 at 201. Binomial is the only engine the panel allows for American exercise (OptionPricerPanel.tsx:246-249 blocks BS and MC there), so every American option's gamma comes from this path. Theta is positive for a long call here and negative under BS.
evidence_checked: Read the CRR pricer, the FD Greeks and the panel's method and steps defaults. Re-ran three POSTs through scripts/r15/vy.py against :52152.
repro_check: vy.py post /quant/option/price (european call S=K=100, r 0.05, vol 0.2, 1y): binomial 200 steps -> gamma 0.0530, theta +6.41; 201 steps -> gamma 8.9e-15; black-scholes -> gamma 0.018762, theta -6.41. Reproduced.

reason: Holds. The batch route fans symbols out with asyncio.to_thread, but every nse_direct call goes through a process-global _lock plus a _Throttle that sleeps ~1.0-1.4 s while holding a worker thread. nse_provider has no quote cache, so an IN batch costs about 1.2 s per symbol, and the watchlist re-polls it every 5 s. The cross-route starvation was not re-measured; it follows from the shared default executor and matches the driver's log.
evidence_checked: Read the batch route, the throttle, the global-lock request path, get_quote (no cache) and the watchlist poll loop. Timed warm batches on :52152.
repro_check: curl ':52152/quotes?symbols=<N .NS names>' warm: N=1 -> 0.15 s (no wait after idle), N=6 -> 7.34 s, N=12 -> 14.61 s. Every row came from nse_direct, a linear ~1.2 s per symbol. The serialisation reproduced; the 9x contention on /quotes/SPY was not re-run.

reason: Holds. _fiscal_period_for maps the report month to the calendar quarter it falls in (Oct -> Q4) and stamps the report's year. It is applied to every EarningsEvent and EarningsEstimateDetail, so a report on the prior quarter is always labelled one quarter late. The earnings_upcoming tool returns event.model_dump(), fiscal_period included, to the model. The panel does not render the field (no non-test .tsx reference), so the harm reaches users through the agent.
evidence_checked: Read the inference function, both call sites and the agent tool's return. Grepped src/modules/earnings for fiscal_period. Re-ran the GET on :52152.
repro_check: curl ':52152/earnings/upcoming?days=60' -> JPM, TSLA, V, GOOGL, META, MSFT all {quarter: Q4, year: 2026} for October reports (JPM's is its Q3; MSFT's is FY27 Q1). Reproduced.

reason: Holds. The yield-curve route maps only ValueError to 400, so QuantLib's RuntimeError on a duplicate pillar propagates as a 500. app.py registers only a ProviderError handler, and a 500 raised past CORSMiddleware carries no CORS header, which is the documented CORS-masks-500 trap. The panel's validationError checks only that each tenor is at least 1 and each rate is positive, never duplicates.
